section_summary: This section contains two brief, poorly legible incoming airgrams, a confidential Tokyo economic report, and a despatch assessing the Economic Stabilization Board’s criticism of the stabilization program. Most pages reproduce the Board’s November 1949 study of prices, credit, trade, employment, investment, and public works. The study continues beyond page 506.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram from Tokyo
subfiles.about: The airgram’s substantive text is illegible in the supplied OCR.
subfiles.summary: Incoming airgram with an illegible body.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-323: economic and trade developments
subfiles.about: Reports confidential observations on economic administration, labor, sterling devaluation, and Japanese trade arrangements.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text discusses silver sales, Dodge’s distrust of leaks from Economic Stabilization Board officials, a draft foreign exchange and trade control law, and a Japanese labor delegation. It also covers an AFL office proposal, trade after sterling devaluation, and proposed arrangements with the Ryukyus and Thailand.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram A-333: economic developments
subfiles.about: Reports on the reparations delegation, a technical white paper, and proposals to expand trade with China.
subfiles.summary: The U.S. reparations delegation is closing. The airgram also notes Japan’s technical white paper and proposals for increasing China trade.

subfiles.title: Further views of Economic Stabilization Board with regard to stabilization program
subfiles.from: U.S. Political Adviser, Tokyo; signed by C. H. Beringer
subfiles.about: Forwards and assesses the Economic Stabilization Board’s study of Japan’s stabilization program.
subfiles.summary: The despatch summarizes the Board’s concern that tight credit and weak investment were stalling recovery. It questions some evidence and conclusions while considering the need for longer term capital, especially for shipping, hydroelectric power, and smaller enterprises. It also discusses the Board’s relationship with the Social Democratic Party.

subfiles.title: Japan’s Economy Since Enforcement of Stabilization Program
subfiles.about: Evaluates the results and economic costs of Japan’s stabilization program.
subfiles.summary: The Board finds that inflation has subsided, prices and wages have stabilized, and some controls and subsidies have been reduced. It argues that weak exports, falling investment, inadequate long term credit, and limited demand threaten production and employment, particularly in capital goods industries and smaller businesses. Detailed tables examine monetary conditions, prices, trade, industrial productivity, equipment funding, and public works. The report continues after page 506.
